details:
I think we seriously need to talk about what's happening with Photon bots in VRChat, especially the accounts advertising **hexed**.

This isn't just about random bots joining public instances anymore. It's becoming a serious concern for player privacy, avatar creators, and communities that simply want to enjoy VRChat without worrying about automated accounts collecting information.

What's happening?

Some accounts appearing in VRChat are openly advertising** hexed**, a website promoting automated Photon bots, avatar databases, reuploading services, and public user lookup features.

Their profiles also claim that banned bot accounts can be automatically replaced.

Think about what that means.

We're potentially dealing with automated clients capable of repeatedly entering instances, collecting information, and continuing their activity even when individual accounts are banned.

Unlike regular players, Photon bots can interact with VRChat's networking systems through automated clients. This makes the issue more complicated than simply dealing with someone using the game normally.

I've attached a screenshot showing one of these accounts and what it advertises.

Whether every advertised capability works exactly as claimed is something VRChat should investigate, but the fact that these services are being promoted inside the platform is already concerning.

Why should players care?

VRChat isn't just another multiplayer game. For many people, it's a place to socialize, build friendships, create communities, and express themselves through their avatars.

Some avatar creators spend hundreds of hours making their models. Others spend significant amounts of money commissioning custom work.

Seeing accounts advertise automated avatar collection and reuploading is understandably frustrating for those creators.

And this goes beyond avatars.

There's a difference between someone viewing publicly available information and automated systems systematically collecting and indexing information about large numbers of players.

Just because certain information is accessible doesn't mean everyone is comfortable with it being collected and distributed through third-party services.

People shouldn't have to constantly question whether someone joining their instance is a real player or an automated client collecting information.

Current moderation tools aren't enough

We can block accounts, report users, vote-kick people, and moderate group instances.

But these tools are mostly reactive.

By the time someone notices a suspicious account, checks its profile, and takes action, it has already entered the instance.

If the claims about automatically replacing banned accounts are accurate, banning individual bots may only temporarily interrupt the activity.

And realistically, community moderators shouldn't have to constantly monitor every account joining an instance.

Yes, we could use Friends or Invite instances, but that defeats the purpose of public communities.

Public instances are where people discover new communities, meet strangers, and make friends.

We shouldn't have to close our instances completely just to feel more protected.

My suggestion: Minimum Trust Rank requirements

I would like VRChat to introduce an optional setting when creating an instance that allows owners to choose the minimum Trust Rank required to join.

For example:

Everyone (default)

New User and above

User and above

Known User and above

Trusted User only

This setting could be available for Public, Group Public, Group+, and other appropriate instance types.

Instance owners and authorized group moderators should also be able to change the restriction while the instance is running.

If someone doesn't meet the requirement, VRChat could display a message such as:

"This instance requires a minimum Trust Rank of User to join."

The minimum rank should also be visible in the instance browser.

For group instances, administrators could configure a default requirement for their events or community spaces.

There should also be an option to allow exceptions for invited friends, group members, or specifically approved players.

This isn't about excluding new players

I want to be clear that this suggestion isn't about treating Visitors or New Users as suspicious.

Everyone starts somewhere, and new players deserve to enjoy VRChat.

That's why the setting should be completely optional and disabled by default.

Communities that want to welcome everyone could continue doing so without changing anything.

Other communities could enable additional restrictions when necessary.

I also understand that Trust Rank doesn't determine whether someone is legitimate. Automated accounts might eventually achieve higher ranks, while legitimate players might remain at lower ranks.

This wouldn't eliminate Photon bots, but it could create an additional barrier against newly generated accounts repeatedly joining instances.

It's about having another option, not pretending that Trust Rank is a perfect anti-bot system.

VRChat should also investigate Photon bot abuse

Minimum Trust Rank restrictions are only part of the solution.

I believe VRChat should also investigate automated clients that appear to be collecting player or avatar information on a large scale, especially services advertising automatic account replacement after bans.

Some additional protections worth considering:

Better detection of coordinated automated account activity and repeated suspicious joins.

Stronger measures against automated ban evasion.

Additional moderation controls for public and group instances.

A dedicated reporting option for suspected Photon bot abuse or automated data collection.

More transparency about which player and avatar information can be accessed through automated clients.

Temporary protection settings for communities hosting public events.

These systems would need to be implemented carefully to avoid falsely flagging legitimate users.

But the current situation shows why relying entirely on individual reports and account bans may not be enough.

Why this matters

What concerns me most isn't just one website.

It's what happens if automated data collection becomes increasingly common across VRChat.

Communities might become less willing to host public events. Avatar creators might become more protective of their work. Players who already have privacy concerns might avoid public instances entirely.

That would be a shame for a platform built around social interaction and creativity.

We should be encouraging people to explore public worlds and meet others, not making them feel like private instances are their only reasonable option.

Final thoughts

I'm not asking VRChat to restrict everyone or treat every new account as a bot.

I'm asking for more control over the instances we create and better preventative protections against automated abuse.

The accounts advertising **hexed** highlight why this issue deserves attention.

When a service openly promotes automated Photon bots, avatar reuploading, and replacement accounts after bans, I think the community has every reason to ask how these activities are being addressed.

Trust Rank restrictions won't fix everything, but they would be a useful additional tool.

We shouldn't always have to wait for suspicious accounts to enter our instances before taking action.

Please consider adding optional minimum Trust Rank requirements alongside stronger protections against automated Photon bot abuse.

VRChat is built around its communities, and giving those communities more control over their spaces would be a meaningful improvement.
title: VRChat Needs Better Instance Protection Against Data-Collecting Bots (hexed)
